input.description: Fix FAT/exFAT audit findings
input.prompt:
You are fixing data-corruption bugs in the FAT and exFAT code of DiskUltimate, a pure-Python disk tool at /home/pc/Belgeler/GitHub/DiskUltimate (read its CLAUDE.md first; it is in Turkish). Other agents are concurrently editing OTHER areas of the same working tree (ext, NTFS, partition tables), so follow the coordination rules below strictly.

## Background
A real-world FAT32 made by mkdosfs (25549 clusters) was misread as FAT16 because tests only used volumes made by our own formatter (already fixed: BPB_FATSz16==0 → FAT32). An audit against mkfs.fat 4.2 / exfatprogs 1.3.2 volumes found (see `.claude/logs/2026-10-06-uyumluluk-denetimi.md`, items F0, X1–X4, F5–F9, X10, X11):

- F0 (c, verified by me): `FatFS.write_file('/yok/a.bin', 300000 bytes)` into a NON-EXISTENT directory allocates clusters, then raises "Yol bulunamadi" → fsck.vfat: "Reclaimed 586 unused clusters", "Free cluster summary wrong". The writer must resolve the parent directory (and check name/space) BEFORE allocating, and roll back allocations on any failure. ExFatFS handles this case correctly — check other failure paths in both (disk full mid-write, dir full on FAT12/16 fixed root, invalid name).
- X1 (c, verified): exFAT directories with NoFatChain (GeneralSecondaryFlags bit1) are read via the FAT: `_read_chain_data(cluster)` (exfat.py ~531,545,556,696,724,845,863) ignores the NoFatChain flag and the directory's DataLength. Linux `exfat_alloc_new_dir` and Windows create NoFatChain directories; FAT entries for them are never written (stale values normal). Test: 3-cluster NoFatChain dir with 127 files → we list 42; one write → fsck checksum errors, 85 files left; new cluster FAT-chained while flag stays NoFatChain; `_set_dir_size` truncated DataLength. Must be fixed for reading AND writing (when extending a NoFatChain directory either keep contiguity or convert it to a FAT chain by writing the chain and clearing the flag — the kernel's `exfat_chain_cont_cluster` does the conversion). Also files: verify NoFatChain files are handled everywhere (read, write/extend, delete, rename, recursive remove, recovery scan).
- X2 (c, verified): exFAT NameLength is counted in code points, not UTF-16 code units (writer exfat.py ~655,673; reader ~515 `name[:name_length]` on a Python str leaves trailing NULs for surrogate pairs). Spec 7.6.3: UTF-16 units. Name hash must also be over UTF-16 units of the upcased name.
- X3 (c): ValidDataLength ignored (only DataLength at offset 24 read, ~508); reads beyond VDL must return zeros; rename (~871 → 675) must preserve VDL instead of writing VDL=DataLength.
- X4 (c): NumberOfFats=2 / TexFAT / VolumeFlags.ActiveFat ignored; `_read_root_metadata` (~303-305) keeps the LAST bitmap entry (should pick BitmapFlags bit0 == ActiveFat). Minimum acceptable: refuse write/resize (and make usedmap return None) when NumberOfFats != 1 or ActiveFat != 0, and pick the correct bitmap for reading.
- F5 (c): FAT12/16 uses the high cluster word at dir-entry offset 0x14 (fat.py ~425, recovery.py ~126); kernel `fat_get_start` uses starthi only on FAT32 (OS/2 stores EA handle there). rename (~859,874-875) re-writes content → data loss.
- F6 (c): FAT32 BPB_ExtFlags (offset 40) ignored: if bit7 set (mirroring disabled), active FAT = bits 0-3; `_load_fat` reads FAT0 and `flush` copies it to every FAT; resize.py ~395-399 and usedmap._fat same. Fix: read/write the active FAT (and only it when mirroring disabled), or at minimum refuse writes/resize and make usedmap use the active FAT.
- F7 (c): lost-partition scan (recovery.py ~276,298-305) mixes sector units: exFAT VolumeLength (units of 2^BytesPerSectorShift) and FAT TotSec (units of BPB_BytsPerSec) taken as device sectors → `session.adopt_lost_partition` (session.py ~1251) creates wrong-size partition. FAT12 reported as FAT16 there (`root != 0`).
- F8 (a): FAT label: root-dir volume-label entry not read (blkid/Windows read it first; "NO NAME" shown literally; extended boot signature 0x29 not checked); `set_label` (fat.py ~878-894) updates only BPB → fsck auto-copies root label back. Backup boot sector hardcoded to sector 6 instead of BPB_BkBootSec (0x32).
- F9 (a): short names decoded latin-1, should be CP437 (0x05 first byte = 0xE5).
- X10 (a): exFAT name matching uses str.lower, should use the volume upcase table.
- X11 (b): exFAT deleted-file recovery assumes contiguous data even when the FAT chain survives.
Checked OK per audit: mkfs.fat -S 4096/-S 2048/-f 1/-s 128/-R 4/-a -r 1024/-M 0xF0 write paths passed fsck; TotSec16 precedence; FAT12/16 threshold; root cluster from BPB; FSInfo guard.

## Your task
1. Fix F0, X1, X2, X3, F5, F7 properly. X4 and F6: proper fix if reasonable, else safety gate (refuse write/resize with clear tr() message; usedmap returns None). F8, F9, X10, X11 if cheap after the rest.
2. Write regression tests in a NEW file `tests/regress_fat.py` (do NOT edit tests/run_all.py). Structure: list of test functions + `main()` printing TAMAM/BASARISIZ/ATLANDI, nonzero exit on failure, runnable as `python3 -m tests.regress_fat`. Build inputs with real tools where possible (mkfs.fat, mkfs.exfat, fsck.vfat -n, fsck.exfat -n, installed locally; mtools is NOT installed locally, no root → no mount). Craft NoFatChain directories/files, VDL<DataLength files, emoji names, ExtFlags-mirroring-off, OS/2 starthi bytes etc. by writing the structures directly where tools can't produce them (exfatprogs: check if `exfat2img`/`tune.exfat`/`dump.exfat` help). After each write, external fsck must return 0. Missing tool → ATLANDI, never a silent pass. Use your own scratch dir: `from diskultimate.paths import scratch; scratch("regress_fat")`.
3. Run your module, the existing FAT/exFAT tests from run_all INDIVIDUALLY (e.g. `python3 -c "import tests.run_all as r; r.t03_fat(); r.cleanup_test_files('t03')"` — find FAT/exFAT ones by grep; do NOT run the whole suite, others share `.tmp/tests`), `python3 -m tests.yabanci --sec fat32,fat16,fat12,exfat --calisma <your scratch>/yab`, and `python3 -m tests.platform_check` (must be 0 findings).

## Coordination rules (important)
- Only edit: fat.py, exfat.py, formatter.py FAT/exFAT parts, the FAT/exFAT parts of fsdetect.py, usedmap.py (`_fat`, `_exfat` only), resize.py (FAT/exFAT parts), recovery.py (FAT/exFAT parts), session.py only if needed for F7, filesystem.py FAT/exFAT access classes. Use targeted Edit operations; never rewrite whole shared files.
- Do NOT edit: tests/run_all.py, i18n catalogs, `.claude/` docs, CLAUDE.md, workflows. Do not commit/push or change git state.
- New user-visible strings: wrap in tr(); list each new source string in your final report.
- CLAUDE.md code rules: core/ no PyQt; no subprocess/shutil.which/tempfile in core/; explicit endianness in struct formats; English function names; Turkish ASCII comments like the surrounding code.

input.prompt:
You are fixing data-corruption bugs in the partition-table code of DiskUltimate, a pure-Python disk tool at /home/pc/Belgeler/GitHub/DiskUltimate (read its CLAUDE.md first; it is in Turkish). Other agents are concurrently editing OTHER areas of the same working tree (ext, FAT/exFAT, NTFS), so follow the coordination rules strictly.

## Background
A real-world FAT32 made by mkdosfs was misread because tests only used volumes/tables produced by our own code. An audit against sfdisk/kernel behaviour found (items P1–P8 in `.claude/logs/2026-10-06-uyumluluk-denetimi.md`):

- P1 (c, reproduced with DiskImage(sector_size=4096)): GPT→MBR on 4Kn disks: `MBRTable.write` builds bytearray(512) (mbr.py ~188,231) so write_sectors raises AFTER `gpt_to_mbr` already zeroed the GPT (convert.py ~176-179) → no table. GPT_RESERVED_HEAD/TAIL (34/33) are 512-byte assumptions; on 4Kn the tail zeroing can hit a last partition ending at N-6 (sfdisk default). `check_gpt_to_mbr` (convert.py ~142) never checks first partition start ≥ 34 (a table-length 4 GPT allows start at LBA 3 which would be zeroed). Conversion must validate everything first, build the new table in memory, and only then write (never destroy the old table before the new one is known to be writable).
- P2 (c, reproduced): `GPTTable.is_present` (gpt.py ~92) checks only "EFI PART"; no 0xEE protective-MBR check and no CRC check. Kernel `efi.c find_valid_gpt` requires a valid PMBR (`is_pmbr_valid`), otherwise msdos parser. Repro: sfdisk GPT (2048,+20480), then overwrite sector 0 with a DOS MBR (2048,+100000): we show the stale GPT, kernel/sfdisk show the MBR; any GPT write then destroys the real MBR; usedmap.disk_used_ranges uses the stale table and silently skips live data in used-only backups.
- P3 (c): `header_crc_ok`/`entries_crc_ok` (gpt.py ~120) unused; corrupt primary trusted and copied over the good backup on next write. Kernel falls back to the alternate header (and checks entries CRC).
- P4 (c, reproduced): slots are renumbered on any table write: `gpt._build_entries` (~167) and `MBRTable.write` (~194) sort+compact (sfdisk GPT slots 1/3/5 → 1/2/3 after a rename; MBR 2/4 → 1/2) — breaks /dev/sdXN in fstab and GRUB (hd0,gpt5). Read side numbering also skips empty slots so displayed numbers differ from the kernel's. Preserve slot positions (new partitions take the first free slot).
- P5 (c): hybrid MBR erased on every GPT write (gpt.py ~206 clears all 4 entries). Preserve an existing hybrid MBR's extra entries (or at least do not destroy it silently: refuse or keep).
- P6 (c, reproduced): `first_usable_lba` (gpt.py ~80) returns max(header, 2048) and write() stores it: an sfdisk table with first-lba 34 and a partition at 34 ends up with a partition before FirstUsableLBA. Keep the header's value for existing tables; only use 2048 as the default for NEW tables / new partition placement. `layoutedit.first_usable` (~164) and `_reserved_before = align` reject such layouts on restore (refusal, lower priority).
- P7 (c): GPT write never checks partitions against the new backup location (gpt.py ~215): on a disk smaller than the table, backup header/entries overwrite the last partition's tail. Refuse.
- P8 (a): images always open with 512-byte sectors (image.py ~242, vdisk.py ~551); a raw 4Kn image shows as an 0xEE MBR. Optional: detect a 4Kn GPT image (EFI PART at byte 4096 and not at 512) and open with sector_size 4096.
- Also (a): EBR parser reads only slot 0 for data and slot 1 for link (kernel scans all 4); partitions past end of disk rejected by PartitionView instead of truncated like the kernel; CHS-only entries show empty.
Checked correct per audit: EBR addressing relative offsets, loop guard, 0x05/0x0F/0x85, LBA-0 fake-entry → whole disk.

## Your task
1. Fix P1, P2, P3, P4, P6, P7 properly. P5: preserve hybrid entries or refuse writes on hybrid MBR disks with a clear tr() message. P8 and the (a) items if cheap.
2. `tests/long` yedek adımı artık iki kipi de dener ve **çöple dolu** hedefe
geri yükler (sıfır hedef, yanlışlıkla atlanan bloğu gizleyebilirdi).

kesilecek bolgede (yeni sonun otesinde) **kullanimdaki** her seyin once

* dosya/dizin veri bloklari, extent agaci dugumleri, dolayli blok tablolari,

* silinecek gruplardaki **inode'lar** — numaralari degisir, bu yuzden onlara

(metadata_csum): inode, extent dugumleri, dizin bloklari, htree dugumleri.
Hepsi yeniden hesaplanir.

Extent kullanan bir dosyanin tasinmasi agaci **bastan kurar**: eski esleme
okunur, kesilen bolgedeki araliklar yeni yerlerine kopyalanir, yeni esleme
gerekirse daha derin bir agacla yazilir. (Ayni yardimci, `extwrite`in
"extent agaci buyutme" eksigi icin de kullanilir: `build_extent_tree`.)

Reddedilenler: `inline_data`, `ea_inode`, kotali birimde inode tasima,
kesilen bolgede kotuk blok (inode 1) kaydi.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import struct
from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Set, Tuple

                        COMPAT_RESIZE_INODE, GD_BLOCK_BITMAP, GD_FLAGS,
                        GD_FREE_BLOCKS, GD_FREE_INODES, GD_INODE_BITMAP,
                        GD_INODE_TABLE, GD_ITABLE_UNUSED, GD_USED_DIRS,
                        INCOMPAT_META_BG, ExtGeometry, raw_crc32c)
from .extresize import (INO_RESIZE, MIN_LAST_GROUP_FREE, ExtResizeError,
                        _build_resize_inode, _set_padding, _Volume,
                        _write_gdt, _write_superblocks, _zero_blocks)

from ..i18n import tr

# inode alanlari
I_MODE, I_SIZE, I_BLOCKS, I_FLAGS, I_BLOCK = 0x00, 0x04, 0x1C, 0x20, 0x28
I_GENERATION, I_FILE_ACL, I_FILE_ACL_HI = 0x64, 0x68, 0x76
S_IFMT, S_IFDIR, S_IFREG, S_IFLNK = 0xF000, 0x4000, 0x8000, 0xA000
EXTENTS_FL = 0x00080000
INDEX_FL = 0x00001000
HUGE_FILE_FL = 0x00040000
INLINE_DATA_FL = 0x10000000
EA_INODE_FL = 0x00200000
EXT_MAGIC = 0xF30A
MAX_INIT_LEN = 32768
MAX_UNINIT_LEN = 32767

INCOMPAT_EA_INODE = 0x0400
INCOMPAT_INLINE_DATA = 0x8000
RO_HUGE_FILE = 0x0008
RO_QUOTA = 0x0100
RO_PROJECT = 0x2000

# ustbloktaki inode numarasi alanlari
SB_INODE_FIELDS = (0xE0, 0x240, 0x244, 0x268, 0x26C, 0x280)
SB_JNL_BLOCKS = 0x10C
SB_JNL_BACKUP_TYPE = 0xFD

Progress = Optional[Callable[[str, int], None]]


# ======================================================================
# Extent agaci
# ======================================================================
def _ext_header(data: bytes, off: int = 0) -> Tuple[int, int, int, int]:
    magic, entries, maximum, depth = struct.unpack_from("<HHHH", data, off)
    if magic != EXT_MAGIC:
        raise ExtResizeError(tr("Extent basligi bozuk"))
    return entries, maximum, depth, off + 12


def read_extents(vol: _Volume, i_block: bytes
                 ) -> Tuple[List[Tuple[int, int, int, bool]], List[int]]:
    """(yapraklar[(mantiksal, uzunluk, fiziksel, baslatilmamis)], dugum_bloklari)."""
    leaves: List[Tuple[int, int, int, bool]] = []
    nodes: List[int] = []

    def walk(buf: bytes, off: int) -> None:
        entries, _max, depth, pos = _ext_header(buf, off)
        for i in range(entries):
            e = pos + i * 12
            if depth == 0:
                lblk, length, hi, lo = struct.unpack_from("<IHHI", buf, e)
                uninit = length > MAX_INIT_LEN
                if uninit:
                    length -= MAX_INIT_LEN
                leaves.append((lblk, length, (hi << 32) | lo, uninit))
            else:
                _lblk, lo, hi = struct.unpack_from("<IIH", buf, e)
                child = (hi << 32) | lo
                nodes.append(child)
                walk(vol.read_block(child), 0)

    walk(i_block, 0)
    return leaves, nodes


def _pack_leaf(entries: List[Tuple[int, int, int, bool]]) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    for lblk, length, pblk, uninit in entries:
        stored = length + (MAX_INIT_LEN if uninit else 0)
        out += struct.pack("<IHHI", lblk, stored, pblk >> 32, pblk & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    return bytes(out)


def _pack_index(entries: List[Tuple[int, int]]) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    for lblk, child in entries:
        out += struct.pack("<IIHH", lblk, child & 0xFFFFFFFF, child >> 32, 0)
    return bytes(out)


def build_extent_tree(vol: _Volume, ino: int, generation: int,
                      extents: List[Tuple[int, int, int, bool]],
                      alloc: Callable[[], int]) -> Tuple[bytes, List[int]]:
    """Yaprak listesinden agac kurar. (i_block[60 bayt], yeni_dugum_bloklari).

    Kok (inode icinde) en fazla 4 giris tasir; asarsa yaprak bloklari, o da
    asarsa ara dizin bloklari eklenir. Her blok `ext4_extent_tail`
    saglamasiyla muhurlenir.
    """
    bs = vol.bs
    per_block = (bs - 12) // 12
    new_nodes: List[int] = []
    level_entries: List = list(extents)
    depth = 0
    while len(level_entries) > 4:
        parents: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []
        for i in range(0, len(level_entries), per_block):
            chunk = level_entries[i:i + per_block]
            blk = alloc()
            new_nodes.append(blk)
            buf = bytearray(bs)
            struct.pack_into("<HHHHI", buf, 0, EXT_MAGIC, len(chunk), per_block,
                             depth, 0)
            body = _pack_leaf(chunk) if depth == 0 else _pack_index(chunk)
            buf[12:12 + len(body)] = body
            _stamp_extent_block(vol, ino, generation, buf, per_block)
            vol.write_block(blk, buf)
            parents.append((chunk[0][0], blk))
        level_entries = parents
        depth += 1
    root = bytearray(60)
    struct.pack_into("<HHHHI", root, 0, EXT_MAGIC, len(level_entries), 4, depth, 0)
    body = _pack_leaf(level_entries) if depth == 0 else _pack_index(level_entries)
    root[12:12 + len(body)] = body
    return bytes(root), new_nodes


def _inode_seed(vol: _Volume, ino: int, generation: int) -> int:
    crc = raw_crc32c(vol.csum.seed, struct.pack("<I", ino))
    return raw_crc32c(crc, struct.pack("<I", generation))


def _stamp_extent_block(vol: _Volume, ino: int, generation: int,
                        buf: bytearray, maximum: int) -> None:
    if vol.csum.kind != "crc32c":
        return
    tail = 12 + 12 * maximum
    crc = raw_crc32c(_inode_seed(vol, ino, generation), bytes(buf[:tail]))
    struct.pack_into("<I", buf, tail, crc)


def _restamp_tree(vol: _Volume, ino: int, generation: int, nodes: List[int]) -> None:
    if vol.csum.kind != "crc32c":
        return
    for blk in nodes:
        buf = vol.read_block(blk)
        _e, maximum, _d, _p = _ext_header(buf)
        _stamp_extent_block(vol, ino, generation, buf, maximum)
        vol.write_block(blk, buf)


# ======================================================================
# Blok tahsisi (kalan bolgede, bellek ici bitmap'lerle)
# ======================================================================
class _Allocator:
    def __init__(self, vol: _Volume, new_geo: ExtGeometry, keep_groups: int):
        self.vol = vol
        self.geo = new_geo
        self.keep_groups = keep_groups
        self.maps: Dict[int, bytearray] = {}
        self.dirty: Set[int] = set()
        self.cursor = 0

    def bitmap(self, group: int) -> bytearray:
        bm = self.maps.get(group)
        if bm is None:
            bm = self.vol.block_bitmap(group)
            # Kesilen son grubun sinirin otesi dolu sayilir (dolgu).
            _set_padding(bm, self.geo.group_block_count(group), self.vol.bs * 8)
            self.maps[group] = bm
        return bm

    def _locate(self, block: int) -> Tuple[int, int]:
        return divmod(block - self.geo.first_data_block, self.geo.blocks_per_group)

    def is_used(self, block: int) -> bool:
        g, i = self._locate(block)
        return bool(self.bitmap(g)[i >> 3] & (1 << (i & 7)))

    def mark(self, block: int, used: bool) -> None:
        g, i = self._locate(block)
        if g >= self.keep_groups or block >= self.geo.blocks_count:
            return                      # kesilen bolge: iz tutulmaz
        bm = self.bitmap(g)
        if used:
            bm[i >> 3] |= 1 << (i & 7)
        else:
            bm[i >> 3] &= ~(1 << (i & 7)) & 0xFF
        self.dirty.add(g)

    def alloc_run(self, want: int) -> Tuple[int, int]:
        """En fazla `want` uzunlugunda bitisik bos aralik: (baslangic, uzunluk)."""
        geo = self.geo
        for step in range(self.keep_groups):
            g = (self.cursor + step) % self.keep_groups
            bm = self.bitmap(g)
            limit = geo.group_block_count(g)
            i = _find_zero(bm, 0, limit)
            while i is not None:
                j = i
                while j < limit and j - i < want and not bm[j >> 3] & (1 << (j & 7)):
                    j += 1
                length = j - i
                if length:
                    start = geo.group_first_block(g) + i
                    for b in range(i, j):
                        bm[b >> 3] |= 1 << (b & 7)
                    self.dirty.add(g)
                    self.cursor = g
                    return start, length
                i = _find_zero(bm, j, limit)
        raise ExtResizeError(tr("Kucultme icin yeterli bos alan yok"))

    def alloc(self) -> int:
        return self.alloc_run(1)[0]

    def alloc_contiguous(self, count: int) -> int:
        """Tam `count` bitisik blok (inode tablosu icin)."""
        geo = self.geo
        for g in range(self.keep_groups):
            bm = self.bitmap(g)
            limit = geo.group_block_count(g)
            i = _find_zero(bm, 0, limit)
            while i is not None:
                j = i
                while j < limit and j - i < count and not bm[j >> 3] & (1 << (j & 7)):
                    j += 1
                if j - i == count:
                    for b in range(i, j):
                        bm[b >> 3] |= 1 << (b & 7)
                    self.dirty.add(g)
                    return geo.group_first_block(g) + i
                i = _find_zero(bm, j, limit)
        raise ExtResizeError(tr("Inode tablosu icin bitisik bos alan yok"))


def _find_zero(bm: bytearray, start: int, limit: int) -> Optional[int]:
    """`start`tan itibaren ilk sifir bit (bayt duzeyinde hizli atlama)."""
    i = start
    while i < limit:
        if i & 7 == 0:
            byte_index = i >> 3
            end_byte = (limit + 7) >> 3
            while byte_index < end_byte and bm[byte_index] == 0xFF:
                byte_index += 1
            i = byte_index << 3
            if i >= limit:
                return None
        if not bm[i >> 3] & (1 << (i & 7)):
            return i
        i += 1
    return None

            return {}
        root = self.vol.read_block(phys[0])
        levels = root[0x1E]
        nodes = {0: 0x20}
        frontier = [(0, 0x20)]
        for _lvl in range(levels):
            nxt = []
            for lblk, off in frontier:
                buf = root if lblk == 0 else self.vol.read_block(phys[lblk])
                _limit, count = struct.unpack_from("<HH", buf, off)
                first = struct.unpack_from("<I", buf, off + 4)[0]
                children = [first] + [struct.unpack_from("<I", buf, off + 8 * k + 4)[0]
                                      for k in range(1, count)]
                for child in children:
                    if child in phys and child not in nodes:
                        nodes[child] = 8
                        nxt.append((child, 8))
            frontier = nxt
        return nodes

    # ---- ana akis ----------------------------------------------------
    def run(self) -> int:
        self.check()
        v = self.vol
        self.report(tr("Kullanilan inode'lar taraniyor..."), 3)
        used = self.used_inodes()
        self.plan_inodes(used)

        # Tasinacak inode'lar silinecek gruplarin tablolarindadir; o tablolar
        # serbest birakilmadan once hepsi bellege alinir.
        self.mover_raw = {ino: self.read_inode(ino) for ino in self.ino_map}
        self.report(tr("Grup metaverisi yerlestiriliyor..."), 8)
        self.relocate_group_metadata()
        self.release_removed_metadata()

        total = max(1, len(used))
        dirs: List[int] = []
        rewritten: Dict[int, bytearray] = {}
        jnl_ino = struct.unpack_from("<I", v.geo.sb, 0xE0)[0] \
            if v.geo.compat & 0x0004 else 0
        orphan_ino = struct.unpack_from("<I", v.geo.sb, 0x280)[0] \
            if v.geo.compat & 0x1000 else 0

            if n % 256 == 0:
                self.report(tr("Veri tasiniyor... {} / {}", n, total),
                            10 + int(60 * n / total))

                continue

            mode = struct.unpack_from("<H", raw, I_MODE)[0]
            links = struct.unpack_from("<H", raw, 0x1A)[0]
            if mode == 0 and links == 0 and ino >= 11:
                continue

            if flags & INLINE_DATA_FL:
                raise ExtResizeError(tr("inline_data inode'u: {}", ino))

                if flags & EXTENTS_FL:

                else:
                    changed = self.move_indirect_file(raw)

                    raise ExtResizeError(tr("Kesilen bolgede kotu blok kaydi var"))

                rewritten[ino] = raw
            if (mode & S_IFMT) == S_IFDIR:
                dirs.append(ino)
            if ino == jnl_ino and changed:
                self._backup_journal_blocks(raw)

        self.report(tr("Inode'lar yaziliyor..."), 72)
        for ino, raw in rewritten.items():
            new_ino = self.ino_map.get(ino)
            if new_ino:
                self._place_inode(ino, new_ino, raw)
            else:
                self.write_inode(ino, raw)

            nodes = self.inode_extents.get(ino)

            for ino in dirs:
                raw = rewritten.get(ino) or self.read_inode(ino)
                self.fix_directory(ino, raw)

                value = struct.unpack_from("<I", v.geo.sb, off)[0]
                if value in self.ino_map:
                    struct.pack_into("<I", v.geo.sb, off, self.ino_map[value])

    def _backup_journal_blocks(self, raw: bytes) -> None:
        sb = self.vol.geo.sb
        if sb[SB_JNL_BACKUP_TYPE] != 1:
            return
        sb[SB_JNL_BLOCKS:SB_JNL_BLOCKS + 60] = raw[I_BLOCK:I_BLOCK + 60]
        struct.pack_into("<I", sb, SB_JNL_BLOCKS + 60,
                         struct.unpack_from("<I", raw, 0x6C)[0])
        struct.pack_into("<I", sb, SB_JNL_BLOCKS + 64,
                         struct.unpack_from("<I", raw, I_SIZE)[0])

    def _restamp_orphan_file(self, ino: int, raw: bytes) -> None:
        if self.vol.csum.kind != "crc32c":
            return
        final = self.ino_map.get(ino, ino)
        generation = struct.unpack_from("<I", raw, I_GENERATION)[0]
        per = (self.bs - 8) // 4
        leaves, _n = read_extents(self.vol, bytes(raw[I_BLOCK:I_BLOCK + 60]))
        for _l, length, pblk, _u in leaves:
            for blk in range(pblk, pblk + length):
                buf = self.vol.read_block(blk)
                if struct.unpack_from("<I", buf, self.bs - 8)[0] != ORPHAN_MAGIC:
                    continue
                crc = raw_crc32c(self.vol.csum.seed, struct.pack("<I", final))
                crc = raw_crc32c(crc, struct.pack("<I", generation))
                crc = raw_crc32c(crc, struct.pack("<Q", blk))
                crc = raw_crc32c(crc, bytes(buf[:per * 4]))
                struct.pack_into("<I", buf, self.bs - 4, crc)
                self.vol.write_block(blk, buf)

    def release_removed_metadata(self) -> None:
        """Silinecek gruplarin kalan bolgedeki metaverisini serbest birakir.

        flex_bg'de 16 grubun inode tablolari ilk grupta durur; buyuk bir
        kucultmede bu alan (4K blokta ~32 MB) tasima icin gereklidir. Guvenli
        olmasi icin tasinacak inode'larin hepsi ONCEDEN belleğe okunmustur
        (`mover_raw`); bu tablolardan bir daha okunmaz.
        """
        v = self.vol
        for gno in range(self.keep, self.old_groups):
            for field, count in ((GD_BLOCK_BITMAP, 1), (GD_INODE_BITMAP, 1),
                                 (GD_INODE_TABLE, self.itb)):
                first = v.d(gno, field)
                for b in range(first, first + count):
                    if not self.in_cut(b):
                        self.alloc.mark(b, False)
        for b in self.freed_gdt:
            self.alloc.mark(b, False)

    def _place_inode(self, old: int, new: int, raw: bytearray) -> None:
        v = self.vol
        gno, idx = divmod(new - 1, self.ipg)
        bm_block = v.d(gno, GD_INODE_BITMAP)
        bm = v.read_block(bm_block)
        bm[idx >> 3] |= 1 << (idx & 7)
        v.write_block(bm_block, bm)
        v.csum.stamp_bitmap(v.descs[gno], bm[:(self.ipg + 7) // 8], True,
                            v.geo.desc_size)
        v.set_d(gno, GD_FREE_INODES, v.d(gno, GD_FREE_INODES) - 1)
        mode = struct.unpack_from("<H", raw, I_MODE)[0]
        if (mode & S_IFMT) == S_IFDIR:
            v.set_d(gno, GD_USED_DIRS, v.d(gno, GD_USED_DIRS) + 1)
        if v.geo.csum_kind:
            unused = v.d(gno, GD_ITABLE_UNUSED)
            v.set_d(gno, GD_ITABLE_UNUSED, min(unused, self.ipg - idx - 1))
        self.write_inode(new, raw)

    def _finish(self) -> None:
        v = self.vol
        new = self.new
        bs = self.bs
        # Kalan gruplarin bitmap'leri yazilir, sayaclar bitmap'ten sayilir.
        for gno in range(self.keep):
            if gno == self.keep - 1 or gno in self.alloc.dirty:
                bm = self.alloc.bitmap(gno)
                length = new.group_block_count(gno)
                _set_padding(bm, length, bs * 8)
                free = _zero_bits(bm, length)
                v.set_d(gno, GD_FREE_BLOCKS, free)
                v.set_d(gno, GD_FLAGS, v.d(gno, GD_FLAGS) & ~BG_BLOCK_UNINIT)
                v.write_block(v.d(gno, GD_BLOCK_BITMAP), bm)
                v.csum.stamp_bitmap(v.descs[gno], bm[:new.blocks_per_group // 8],
                                    False, new.desc_size)
        del v.descs[self.keep:]

        old_r = v.sb_u64(0x08, 0x154)
        old_geo = v.geo
        new.sb[:] = old_geo.sb                    # inode alani duzeltmeleri dahil
        v.geo = new
        struct.pack_into("<H", new.sb, 0xCE, new.reserved_gdt)
        v.sb_set_u64(0x04, 0x150, self.target)
        v.sb_set_u64(0x08, 0x154, old_r * self.target // max(1, self.old_blocks))
        v.sb_set_u64(0x0C, 0x158, sum(v.d(i, GD_FREE_BLOCKS) for i in range(self.keep)))
        v.sb_set_u32(0x10, sum(v.d(i, GD_FREE_INODES) for i in range(self.keep)))
        v.sb_set_u32(0x00, self.ipg * self.keep)
        if new.compat & COMPAT_RESIZE_INODE:
            _build_resize_inode(v)
        _write_gdt(v)
        _write_superblocks(v)
        flush = getattr(self.dev, "flush", None)
        if flush:
            flush()


def _merge_extents(extents: List[Tuple[int, int, int, bool]]
                   ) -> List[Tuple[int, int, int, bool]]:
    out: List[Tuple[int, int, int, bool]] = []
    for lblk, length, pblk, uninit in extents:
        if out:
            pl, plen, pp, pu = out[-1]
            cap = MAX_UNINIT_LEN if uninit else MAX_INIT_LEN
            if pu == uninit and pl + plen == lblk and pp + plen == pblk \
                    and plen + length <= cap:
                out[-1] = (pl, plen + length, pp, pu)
                continue
        out.append((lblk, length, pblk, uninit))
    return out


def _zero_bits(bm: bytes, nbits: int) -> int:
    full, rest = divmod(nbits, 8)
    ones = sum(bin(b).count("1") for b in bm[:full])
    if rest:
        ones += bin(bm[full] & ((1 << rest) - 1)).count("1")
    return nbits - ones


def _is_dirent_tail(buf: bytes, bs: int) -> bool:
    pos = bs - 12
    ino, rec_len, name_len, ftype = struct.unpack_from("<IHBB", buf, pos)
    return ino == 0 and rec_len == 12 and name_len == 0 and ftype == 0xDE

def min_blocks_for(vol: _Volume) -> int:
    """Kucultmenin inebilecegi yaklasik en kucuk blok sayisi.

    Gereken = kullanilan veri bloklari (metaveri disinda) + tasima payi.
    Kullanilan inode'lar da kalan gruplara sigmali. Pay: tasinan dosyalarin
    yeni extent dugumleri ve parcalanma icin %2 + 256 blok.
    """
    g = vol.geo
    itb = g.inode_table_blocks
    meta_total = sum(g.base_meta_count(gno) + 2 + itb for gno in range(g.group_count))
    free = vol.sb_u64(0x0C, 0x158)
    data = max(0, g.blocks_count - free - meta_total)
    need = data + data // 50 + 256
    used_inodes = struct.unpack_from("<I", g.sb, 0x00)[0] - \
        struct.unpack_from("<I", g.sb, 0x10)[0]
    min_groups = max(1, (used_inodes + g.inodes_per_group - 1) // g.inodes_per_group)
    capacity = 0
    for gno in range(g.group_count):
        overhead = g.base_meta_count(gno) + 2 + itb
        room = g.blocks_per_group - overhead
        if gno + 1 >= min_groups and capacity + room >= need:
            last_needed = overhead + max(need - capacity, MIN_LAST_GROUP_FREE + 1)
            return min(g.blocks_count, g.group_first_block(gno) + last_needed)
        capacity += room
    return g.blocks_count


def ext_shrink(dev: BlockDevice, new_size_bytes: int,
               progress: Progress = None) -> int:
    """ext birimini `new_size_bytes`a kucultur. `dev` ESKI boyuttaki penceredir.

    Donus: yeni blok sayisi. Tasima gerekirse yapilir; yetmezse hata verir
    ve birime dokunulmaz (hata, yazmadan onceki denetimlerde cikar).
    """
    vol = _Volume(dev)
    vol.check_supported()
    g = vol.geo
    target = new_size_bytes // g.block_size
    if target >= g.blocks_count:
        return g.blocks_count
    minimum = min_blocks_for(vol)
    if target < minimum:
        raise ExtResizeError(tr(
            "ext birimi bu boyuta kucultulemez; en az {} blok gerekli", minimum))
    # Son grup cok kucuk kalacaksa grup sinirina yuvarlanir (resize2fs gibi)
    trial = ExtGeometry(bytes(g.sb))
    trial.set_blocks_count(target)
    last = trial.group_count - 1
    overhead = trial.base_meta_count(last) + 2 + trial.inode_table_blocks
    if last and trial.group_block_count(last) <= overhead + MIN_LAST_GROUP_FREE:
        target = trial.group_first_block(last)
    return _Shrinker(dev, target, progress).run()

def build_layout(image: BlockDevice, table: PartitionTable) -> EditableLayout:
    """Yedek goruntusunun tablosundan yerlesim cikarir (hedef = kaynak).

    Dosya sistemi sinirlari yedegin icinden okunur; NTFS'te `$Bitmap`
    taranir, yani buyuk yedekte birkac saniye surebilir — arka planda
    cagrilir.
    """
    from .fsdetect import detect

    layout = EditableLayout(scheme=table.scheme,
                           sector_size=image.sector_size,
                           source_sectors=image.sector_count,
                           target_sectors=image.sector_count)
    if isinstance(table, GPTTable):
        layout.gpt_first_usable = table._first_usable
        layout.gpt_entry_sectors = table.entry_sectors
    for part in table.sorted_partitions():
        if not part.logical and part.scheme == "mbr" and \
                part.type_id in MBR_EXTENDED_TYPES:
            layout.extended = copy.copy(part)
            continue
        view = PartitionView(image, part.start_lba, part.sector_count)
        try:
            found = detect(view)
            fs_type, label = found.fs_type, found.label
            part.fs_used = found.used_bytes
        except Exception:                             # noqa: BLE001
            fs_type, label = "", ""
        info = fs_resize_info(view, fs_type)
        item = Slot(part=copy.copy(part), old_start=part.start_lba,
                    old_count=part.sector_count, new_start=part.start_lba,
                    new_count=part.sector_count, fs_type=fs_type, label=label)
        # Geri yuklemede bolum kopyalanir: baslangic her zaman tasinabilir
        item.apply_limits(info.kind, info.min_sectors, info.max_sectors,
                          info.note, movable=True)
        layout.parts.append(item)
    return layout


def _read_table(device: BlockDevice) -> Optional[PartitionTable]:
    if GPTTable.is_present(device):
        return GPTTable.read(device)
    # Onyukleme sektoru de 0x55AA ile biter: tek bolum yedeginin (FAT/NTFS)
    # onyukleme kodu bolum girisi diye okunmasin.
    if MBRTable.is_present(device) and MBRTable.entries_plausible(device):
        return MBRTable.read(device)
    return None


def read_layout(src_path: str) -> Optional[EditableLayout]:
    """`.dub` yedeginin yerlesimi; bolum tablosu yoksa None."""
    image = DubImage(src_path)
    try:
        table = _read_table(image)
        if table is None or not table.partitions:
            return None
        return build_layout(image, table)
    finally:
        image.close()

class _Overlay(BlockDevice):
    """Salt okunur bir aygitin ustunde bellekte duran yazma katmani.

    Kucultme, dosya sisteminin meta verisini (FAT/bitmap, NTFS'te sondan
    tasinan kumeler) yeniden yazar. Yedek dosyasi salt okunurdur; yazilar
    burada tutulur ve okumada yedegin uzerine bindirilir.
    """

    def __init__(self, base: BlockDevice):
        self._base = base
        self.sector_size = base.sector_size
        self._chunks: Dict[int, bytearray] = {}

    @property
    def sector_count(self) -> int:
        return self._base.sector_count

    @property
    def overlay_bytes(self) -> int:
        return len(self._chunks) * OVERLAY_CHUNK

    def _chunk(self, no: int) -> bytearray:
        data = self._chunks.get(no)
        if data is None:
            start = no * OVERLAY_CHUNK
            length = min(OVERLAY_CHUNK, self.size - start)
            data = bytearray(self._base.read(start, length))
            self._chunks[no] = data
        return data

    def read(self, offset: int, length: int) -> bytes:
        if offset + length > self.size:
            raise RestorePlanError(tr("Okuma bolum sinirini asiyor"))
        out = bytearray()
        pos = offset
        end = offset + length
        while pos < end:
            no, inner = divmod(pos, OVERLAY_CHUNK)
            n = min(OVERLAY_CHUNK - inner, end - pos)
            data = self._chunks.get(no)
            if data is not None:
                out += data[inner:inner + n]
            else:
                # yazilmamis parcalar tek okumada birlestirilir
                run = n
                while pos + run < end and \
                        (pos + run) // OVERLAY_CHUNK not in self._chunks:
                    run += min(OVERLAY_CHUNK, end - pos - run)
                out += self._base.read(pos, run)
                n = run
            pos += n
        return bytes(out)

    atlanan alana yazmis olabilir.

        return lambda off, n: src._dev.is_skipped(base + off, n)

1) ntfs-c64k (mkntfs -c 65536) and ntfs-c2m (-c 2097152): after our write (mkdir + 6 files + remove 5 + rename) → `ntfsfix -n`: "$MFTMirr does not match $MFT (record 9)" (also records 6, 8 after our grow; with 2M clusters it lists many records up to 396) → ntfs-3g refuses to mount. So N5 also hits 64K clusters (mirror count = cluster_size/record_size = 64 records), not only >=128K. Please make sure your regression test covers reading a kernel/ntfs-3g-populated -s 4096 volume (ntfscp can populate it without root: many files so directories get $INDEX_ALLOCATION) and compares content.
No reply needed; just include these in your fixes and report.

input.prompt:
You are fixing two bugs in DiskUltimate, a pure-Python disk tool at /home/pc/Belgeler/GitHub/DiskUltimate (read its CLAUDE.md first; Turkish). Other agents concurrently edit ext, FAT/exFAT, NTFS and partition-table code in the same working tree — only touch the files listed below.

Both bugs were found by our new foreign-input matrix (`tests/yabanci`, run on GitHub Actions with real mkfs tools, files written by the Linux kernel, verified with fsck + kernel mount; see `tests/yabanci/__main__.py` and `variants.py`).

## Bug 1 — XFS grow on 1 KiB block size corrupts the reverse-mapping btree
Variant `xfs-b1024`: `mkfs.xfs -q -f -b size=1024 -L YABANCI part.img` (512 MiB), populated by the kernel, partition then grown by our tool (`DiskSession.resize_partition` → XFS grow, code in `src/diskultimate/core/xfsgrow.py`, maybe `xfs.py`/`resize.py` XFS parts). After grow, `xfs_repair -n -f` reports:
```
Reverse Mapping BTree record corruption in AG 4 detected ...
Owner 0xfffffffffffffffd, flags 0x0, start block 0x0 block count 0x1
Could not read reverse-mapping record for (4/0).
```
Owner -3 = XFS_RMAP_OWN_FS (AG headers). With 1 KiB blocks the AG header sectors (sb, agf, agi, agfl = 4 × sector size) span 2+ blocks, but we seem to write block count 1 (fine for 4 KiB blocks). Check every place in the grow path that assumes headers fit in one block (XFS_AGFL_BLOCK, first free block in the new AG, bnobt/cntbt free extent start, rmapbt/refcountbt/finobt root block numbers, AGFL), compare with xfsprogs `xfs_growfs`/kernel `xfs_ag_init_headers`/`xfs_rmaproot_init` for different block and sector sizes. Also check the varyant `xfs-varsayilan` (4 KiB) still passes. Verify locally: mkfs.xfs and xfs_repair are installed (no root, so populate with `mkfs.xfs -p <protofile or dir>` if supported, else test on an empty filesystem plus our tool's own files). Test also block sizes 2048 and 512-sector vs 4096-sector (`-s size=4096`), `-m rmapbt=0/1`, `-m reflink=0/1`, `-m crc=0` (v4) if mkfs allows.

## Bug 2 — HFS+ listing misses a Greek file name
Variants `hfsplus-varsayilan` (`mkfs.hfsplus -v YABANCI part.img`) and `hfsplus-gunluk` (`-J`): kernel hfsplus driver created, among ~360 files, `/belgeler/alt dizin/Ελληνικά αρχεία.bin`. Our listing of that directory (FileSystemAccess.listdir walking all dirs; names compared after `unicodedata.normalize("NFC")` on both sides) does not contain it; all other names (Turkish, Russian, Japanese, emoji-free) are fine. Greek letters with tonos (ά U+03AC, ί U+03AF) are stored decomposed by HFS+ (Apple's decomposition rules; kernel `hfsplus_asc2uni` with its own tables). input.message:
Evidence from the GitHub foreign-input matrix (real mkfs.fat volumes, kernel-populated): FAT resize breaks volumes whose logical sector size != 512:
- fat16-S2048 (`mkfs.fat -F 16 -S 2048`, 128 MiB): after our partition GROW, `fsck.vfat -n` fails with "Seek to 537843712:Invalid argument" (offset far beyond the volume → BPB total-sectors or FAT/data layout written in 512-byte units instead of BPB_BytsPerSec units, or vice versa).
- fat12-S4096 (`mkfs.fat -F 12 -S 4096`, 32 MiB): after our SHRINK, same "Seek to 67383296: Invalid argument".
Please audit resize.py FAT paths (fat_resize, _fat_layout_for, _fat_write_bpb, _fat_max_total, _fat_info min/max, the move path / hidden sectors patching) and usedmap._fat for unit mixing between device sectors (512) and BPB bytes-per-sector, and add regression tests for -S 1024/2048/4096 with FAT12/16/32 grow + shrink + move verified by fsck.vfat -n. (The matrix also confirmed: fat32 group still running; FAT write/read on -S 4096 passed for FAT32.) No reply needed.

  Both bugs are fixed. The new test file catches each bug on the old code and passes on the fixed code. One problem is not fixed: the Linux kernel still can't look up Greek-accented names that our HFS+ writer creates (explained at the end).
  
  ## Bug 1 — XFS grow with small blocks / big sectors (`src/diskultimate/core/xfsgrow.py`)
  **Root cause:**
  - **Fixed layout.** `_layout` (old ~l.148) hard-coded `bno=1, cnt=2, ino=3` and `_rmap_records` (old l.175) wrote `(0, 1, OWN_FS)`. This assumes the four AG header sectors (superblock, AGF, AGI, AGFL) fit in block 0. With 1 KiB blocks and 512 B sectors they take 2 blocks, so the new AG's bnobt root was written over AGI/AGFL and the OWN_FS rmap record was 1 block too short. The 2048 B block size is not affected, but 1024/1024 is.
  - **Superblock CRC on 4 KiB sectors.** The superblock CRC covered only 512 bytes (old l.387 `_crc(primary[:512])`). The kernel computes it over the whole sector, so any `-s size=2048/4096` volume ended up with "bad CRC in superblock" after a grow.
  
  **Fix:**
  - l.153: `agfl_block = (3*sectsize)//bs`. bno/cnt/ino/finobt/rmap/refcount/prealloc now follow `XFS_AGFL_BLOCK+1…`, as in the kernel's `xfs_format.h`.

Picozed.img'deki FAT16 durumu gibi başka kritik hatalar olabilir mi sorusuna kısa cevap: **evet, var ve bir kısmı veri bozabilecek düzeyde**. Hepsi aynı kör noktadan çıkıyor: testlerimiz yalnızca kendi ürettiğimiz birimleri gördü. Düzeltmeler sürüyor; aşağıdakiler şu ana kadar bulunanlar.

**1. picozed.img'in kendisi**
- **Okuma doğru:** FAT32'deki 4 dosya ve ext4'teki 4.370 dosya, referans okuyucularla (ext4 için `debugfs`, FAT için kodumuzdan bağımsız bir okuyucu) bayt bayt aynı; 678 sembolik bağ da tam. Tür ve etiket blkid ile birebir.
- **FAT32 bölümünün kendisi bozuk:** Her iki FAT tablosunun ilk sektöründe, önceki bir biçimlendirmeden kalan önyükleme sektörü baytları var. `fsck.fat` bu yüzden birimi reddediyor, 7-Zip de içinde dosya göremiyor.
  - **Büyük olasılıkla DiskUltimate'ten gelmiyor:** Dosyaların küme zincirleri tam da bu çöp girdileri atlıyor; yani çöp, dosyalar yazılmadan önce oradaydı. Görüntünün son değişiklik tarihi (10 Eylül) deponun ilk commit'inden (14 Eylül) önce ve uygulama kaynağı salt okunur açıyor. Ancak 0.3.0'dan önceki, sürüm kontrolü dışındaki bir prototipin etkisini kesin olarak dışlayamam.
- **Bizim açığımız:** Referans araçlar birimi reddederken program onu sorunsuz bir FAT32 gibi gösterdi ve yazmaya izin verirdi. FAT için tutarlılık denetimi ekletiyorum: böyle bir birim okunabilecek, ama yazma, boyutlandırma ve kullanılan alan yedeği reddedilecek ve arayüzde uyarı çıkacak.

**2. Aynı sınıftan diğer kritik hatalar**
Dört alanı (FAT/exFAT, ext, NTFS, bölüm tabloları) Linux çekirdeği, e2fsprogs, ntfs-3g ve sfdisk davranışına karşı denetlettim. GitHub'daki yeni test matrisi bunlara ek bulgular çıkardı. Veri bozabilecek olanlardan bazıları:
- **FAT:**
  - Olmayan bir klasöre yazma, kümeleri sahipsiz bırakıyor.
  - 2048/4096 baytlık mantıksal sektörlü birimde büyütme ya da küçültme birimi bozuyor.
- **exFAT:** Linux ve Windows'un oluşturduğu dizinlerin bir türü yanlış okunuyor; 127 dosyalık bir dizinde 42 dosya görünüyor ve yazınca dosyalar kayboluyor.
- **ext4:**
  - Yazıcı yalnızca bilinen sorunlu özellikleri reddediyor. Günlüğü işlenmemiş birime yazıyor, sabit bağlı dosyayı silerken diğer adı da bozuyor.
  - inline_data birimlerinde okuma çöküyor.
- **NTFS:**
  - Windows'un Hızlı Başlangıç ile kapattığı birime yazmaya izin veriliyor.
  - 64 KiB ve üstü kümede yazdıktan sonra ntfs-3g birimi bağlamıyor.
  - 4K sektörlü birimlerde dosyalar görünmüyor ya da yanlış okunuyor.
- **Bölüm tabloları:** Eski bir GPT geçerli bir MBR'nin önüne geçiyor. Her tablo yazımında bölüm numaraları kayıyor; bu fstab ve GRUB'u bozar.
- **XFS:** 1 KiB blokta büyütme birimi bozuyor.
- **HFS+:** Yunanca aksanlı bir dosya adı listede görünmüyor.

Tam liste `.claude/logs/2026-10-06-uyumluluk-denetimi.md` içinde.

**Şu an yapılanlar:**
- **Düzeltmeler:** Beş alt ajan paralel çalışıyor; her biri gerçek `mkfs` araçlarıyla regresyon testi yazıyor. Karmaşık durumlarda önce "birimi bozmak yerine reddet" kapısı konuyor. Yazıcıların bilinen sorunları dışlamak yerine yalnızca doğrulanmış özellik ve durumlara izin vermesi yeni kural oldu (ADR 0094).
- **GitHub'daki testler:** Yabancı girdi matrisinin ilk koşusu bitti: 8 gruptan 2'si temiz geçti, 6'sında yukarıdaki hatalar çıktı. Uzun testler (tam profil, 3 platform) hâlâ koşuyor. Matrise sabit bağ, aygıt düğümü, sembolik bağ, seyrek dosya ve casefold dizini gibi özel nesneler de eklendi; denetimin bulduğu hataları artık otomatik yakalayacak.

Düzeltmeler gelince tümünü birleştirip GitHub'da saatlerce sürecek bir tur (`--tur 10`) başlatacağım.

XFS/HFS+ ajanı bitirdi. İki hata da kök nedeniyle düzeltildi; yeni test dosyası her ikisini eski kodda yakalayıp yeni kodda geçiyor (14/14):

- **XFS:** Büyütme, AG başlıklarının tek bloğa sığdığını varsayıyordu. 1 KiB blokta yeni AG'nin kökleri başlıkların üzerine yazılıyordu. 2048/4096 baytlık sektörlerde ise süperblok CRC'si yalnızca 512 bayt üzerinden hesaplanıyordu. İkisi de çekirdek formülüne göre düzeltildi; 11 blok/sektör/özellik bileşiminde büyütme `xfs_repair` ile temiz çıkıyor.
- **HFS+:** Linux sürücüsü Apple'ın eski Unicode 2.1 tablosunu kullanıyor ve Yunanca tonos'u U+030D ile saklıyor; okuyucumuz bunu tanıyamıyordu. Artık her iki biçimi de okuyor, buluyor, yeniden adlandırıyor ve siliyor.

Açık kalan bir tercih var. HFS+ yazıcımız adları macOS'un kullandığı biçimde (TN1150, Unicode 3.2) saklıyor. Linux çekirdeği bizim yazdığımız tonos'lu Yunanca adları bu yüzden bulamıyor. Tek bir biçim iki tarafa birden uymuyor. HFS+ bir Mac dosya sistemi olduğu için macOS biçimini koruyorum ve bu sınırı not ediyorum. Uzun testlerin durumunu da izlemeye alıyorum.

  - **P3 – fixed.** `read` uses the primary if it is valid, otherwise the backup, found at the primary's alternate LBA or N-1. It sets `primary_ok` and `header_backup_ok`, and the next write repairs the primary from the good copy.
  - **P4 – fixed.**
    - GPT: the index is the entry slot. Writes keep the slots and new partitions take the first free slot (`_assign_slots` `:379`).
    - MBR: primaries keep slots 1–4. Logicals are numbered from 5 in chain order, as the kernel does.
    - MBR→GPT keeps the numbers the way gdisk does (1, 5, 6 stay 1, 5, 6).
    - Invalid GPT entries (start > end, or past the end of the disk) are hidden, as the kernel does, but kept byte-for-byte on write.
  - **P5 – preserved, with refusal.** On a hybrid disk sector 0 is left untouched. If a write would remove or change a GPT partition that is mirrored in the hybrid MBR, it is refused (`_protective_sector` `:458`). Create and convert still write a fresh protective MBR.
  - **P6 – fixed.** `first_usable_lba` (`:245`) keeps the header's value; 2048 is only the default for new tables. `layoutedit.first_usable` (`:159`) keeps the table's value. `_reserved_before` (`:192`) uses the real EBR gap for logicals that are not moved.
  - **P7 – fixed.** `build()` (`:490`) checks everything before writing anything: partitions against the first and last usable LBA (that is, the new backup location), overlaps, and the hybrid MBR. `session.resize_image` refuses a shrink that would cut a partition, before truncating.
  - **P8 – done.** `vdisk._raw_sector_size` (`:547`) opens a raw image as 4096 when "EFI PART" is at byte 4096 and not at 512. A blank 4Kn image cannot be detected, so it still opens as 512.
  - **(a) EBR – done.** All 4 EBR slots are scanned for the data entry and the link (`mbr.py:145`).
  - **(a) not done:**
    - Truncating partitions that run past the end of the disk: that code is in `PartitionView`/`session.view`, outside my scope.
    - CHS-only entries: not changed, because the kernel ignores them too.
  
  ### Other behaviour changes
  - `session.create_table("mbr")` now zeroes leftover GPT structures first (`_zero_gpt_remnants`). Otherwise the new MBR would be flagged as ambiguous.
  - `MBRTable.build()` and `GPTTable.build()` are new; they validate and return the writes without touching the disk.
  - Tables our own code creates behave as before, except that numbers no longer shift after a delete or convert.
  
  ### Tests added
  `tests/regress_ptable.py`. Inputs are made with real `sfdisk` (including `--sector-size 4096`) and checked against `sfdisk -J` and `sfdisk -V` before and after our rename/add/delete/resize/type/boot/convert:
  - GPT slots 1/3/5 and MBR slots 2/4 kept
  - logicals 5/6, and an EBR with its entries swapped
  - stale GPT under a DOS MBR, and usedmap not returning None on a clean table
  - corrupt primary entries or header
  - first-lba 34
  - refusal when a partition would overlap the backup GPT, and a refused image shrink
  - hybrid MBR kept, and hybrid-partition delete refused
  - 4Kn image opening, 4Kn GPT→MBR with the last partition ending at N-6
  - table-length 4 GPT with a partition at LBA 3
  - our own 4Kn and 512 tables, MBR→GPT numbering
  
  ### New tr() source strings
  - "Birincil GPT basligi bozuk; tablo yedek basliktan okundu"
  - "Hibrit MBR'de GPT'de olmayan bir alan var (LBA {})"
  - "Bolum {} GPT giris dizisiyle cakisiyor (ilk kullanilabilir LBA {}); tablo yazilmadi"
  - "Bolum {} disk sonundaki yedek GPT alanina tasiyor (son kullanilabilir LBA {}); tablo yazilmadi"
  - "{} ve {} numarali bolumler cakisiyor"
  - "Diskte hibrit MBR var ve bu degisiklik hibrit MBR'de de kayitli bir bolumu (LBA {}) etkiliyor. Hibrit MBR'yi bozmamak icin tablo yazilmadi; once hibrit MBR'yi kaldirin (gdisk)."
  - "Bolum {} gecersiz konumda (LBA {})"
  - "Diskte koruyucu/hibrit MBR girisi (0xEE) var; MBR'den GPT'ye donusturulemez"
  - "Bolum {} LBA 0'da basliyor; MBR bu yerlesimi tasiyamaz"
  - "Koruyucu MBR (0xEE) var ama gecerli GPT basligi bulunamadi"
  - "Diskte MBR'nin yaninda eski bir GPT kalintisi var"
  - "Bolum {} yeni boyutun disinda kaliyor; goruntu kucultulmedi"
  - Progress messages, previously not wrapped: "Mevcut bolumler okunuyor...", "GPT olusturuluyor...", "MBR yaziliyor...", "GPT yapilari siliniyor..."
  
  The catalogs are not updated. `--write <dil>` needs to be run for each language.
  
  ### Other problems found (not fixed)
  - `planview.next_index` still predicts the new partition number as max+1, while the real number is now the first free slot. The preview number can differ (e.g. after a delete); queued steps use LBA anchors, so this is only cosmetic. Not my file.
  - `restoreplan.restore_with_layout` still drops a hybrid MBR from the backup without warning, because it builds a fresh table.
  - The old GPT name truncation was 70 bytes (35 characters); it is now 72.
  - An old backup header left in the middle of a grown image is not wiped; this was already the case before.

The one failure, **ext4-N64**, comes from the harness: debugfs runs out of inodes, prints "Could not allocate inode" and still exits 0, so the manifest lists files the volume doesn't contain (debugfs `ls` shows them missing too). Our reader matches the real contents; the fix belongs in `tests/yabanci`.
  - **i18n_check:** reports missing translations for the strings below, as expected.
  
  ### New tr() strings
  - extwrite.py:
    - `Ayni adda dosya olmayan bir oge var: {}`
    - `Birim coklu baglama korumasi (mmp) kullaniyor; baska bir makinede bagli olabilir. Yazma reddedildi.`
    - `Birim temiz degil (temiz kapatilmamis, hata kaydi ya da islenmemis yetim inode var); bitmap'lere guvenilemez. Once e2fsck ile denetleyin.`
    - `Birimin gunlugunde islenmemis kayitlar var (needs_recovery: temiz kapatilmamis). Yazilirsa cekirdek baglarken gunlugu yazdiklarimizin uzerine oynatir. Once birimi Linux'ta baglayip duzgun ayirin veya e2fsck ile onarin.`
    - `Bu bir ext gunluk aygiti (journal_dev); dosya sistemi degildir, icine yazilamaz.`
    - `Bu birim su ozellikleri kullaniyor ve bu surumde yazma desteklenmiyor: {}. Yanlis yazip birimi bozmamak icin islem reddedildi.` (was not wrapped in tr() before)
    - `Bu klasor buyuk/kucuk harf duyarsiz (casefold); bu surumde icine ad eklenemez.`
    - `Dizin indeksi bozuk: inode {}`
    - `Klasor degistirilemez (immutable) olarak isaretli.`
    - `Klasorde en fazla {} alt klasor olabilir`
    - `Oge degistirilemez (immutable/append-only) olarak isaretli: {}`
    - `inline_data dizinine yazma desteklenmiyor`
  - extmove.py:
    - `Birimde stable_inodes ozelligi var: inode numaralari degistirilemez. Birimi, silinecek gruplarda dosya kalmayacak boyuta kucultun.`
  
  ### Effect on volumes our own formatter makes
  Nothing breaks. Our ext2/3/4 volumes, including `modern=False`, stay writable and keep the same detected type (checked in r05/r14, and all existing tests pass). Visible differences:
  - Overwriting a file now keeps its mode, uid and gid instead of resetting to 0644 and root.
  - On mke2fs volumes, the fs type shown can change where the old rule was wrong: for example `-O ^extent,^huge_file` with flex_bg is now ext4, not ext3.

  - **E3, E13: fixed.** New `ExtInode.has_block_map` and `is_fast_symlink` (fast means size < 60). `_release_data` now skips devices, FIFOs, sockets, fast symlinks and inline inodes.
  - **E4: fixed.** `ExtDirEntry.raw_name` holds the on-disk bytes. The directory entry is removed first (matched by raw name and inode), and only then are blocks freed.
  - **E5: gated.** On casefold volumes the writer can still write, but adding a name inside a CASEFOLD_FL directory is refused (`_check_can_add`, called before anything is allocated).
  - **E6: fixed.** `extmove.plan_inodes` refuses a shrink on stable_inodes volumes when inodes would have to move.
  - **E7: fixed for xattr blocks** (`_release_xattr_block`: decrements refcount, restamps the checksum, frees the block at 0). **EA inodes are gated**: ea_inode volumes are refused.
  - **E10: fixed.**
    - rename keeps the entry's type byte and now adds the new name before removing the old one.
    - The type byte is written as 0 when the filetype feature is off; before, this produced corruption e2fsck flags.
    - dir_nlink follows kernel rules in mkdir and rmdir.
    - `_dir_blocks` keeps holes as 0, and all callers skip them.
    - `read_dir` now parses block by block, so entries after a hole are no longer lost.
  - **E11: fixed.** A zero indirect pointer now becomes a run of zeros.
  - **E12: fixed.** Unwritten extents read as zeros (new `_extent_map`).
  - **E14: fixed for reading.** Inline files of any size, inline directories (including entries continued in `system.data`) and inline symlinks all work through listdir, read, iter_read and extract. No recursion. Writing stays refused.
  - **E15: fixed.** `ext_kind` uses the blkid rule.
  
  ### Extras beyond the list
  - Slow symlinks were unreadable before: `symlink_target` called `read_data`, which rejects symlinks.
  - Overwriting a symlink, device or FIFO through `write_stream` is now refused; before it left an S_IFREG inode with a mismatched entry type.
  - Remove, rename and overwrite are refused on immutable/append-only inodes or parent directories.
  - Test note: DiskImage buffers writes, so e2fsck must run after `flush()`; otherwise it reports false free-count errors.
  
  ### Tests
  `tests/regress_ext.py` (r01–r14) builds every input with mke2fs/debugfs and runs `e2fsck -fn` after each write; a missing tool gives ATLANDI. The inline directory whose entries continue into the xattr is hand-built, because libext2fs never makes one; e2fsck and debugfs both accept it.
  - **Results:** 14/14 TAMAM. Against the HEAD code the same module fails 14/14.
  - **run_all ext tests (run individually, 15):** t05, t16, t19, t31, t47, t48, t51, t53, t54, t55, t73, t74, t79, t89, t93 all TAMAM.
  - **ext_write_check:** 4/4. **ext_resize_check:** 32/32. **platform_check:** 0 findings.
  - **yabanci `--sec ext2,ext3,ext4`:** 23/24 pass. ext4-inline now passes oku, yedek and boyut. The one failure, **ext4-N64**, comes from the harness: debugfs runs out of inodes, prints "Could not allocate inode" and still exits 0, so the manifest lists files the volume doesn't contain (debugfs `ls` shows them missing too). Our reader matches the real contents; the fix belongs in `tests/yabanci`.
  - **i18n_check:** reports missing translations for the strings below, as expected.
  
  ### New tr() strings
  - extwrite.py:
    - `Ayni adda dosya olmayan bir oge var: {}`
    - `Birim coklu baglama korumasi (mmp) kullaniyor; baska bir makinede bagli olabilir. Yazma reddedildi.`
    - `Birim temiz degil (temiz kapatilmamis, hata kaydi ya da islenmemis yetim inode var); bitmap'lere guvenilemez. Once e2fsck ile denetleyin.`
    - `Birimin gunlugunde islenmemis kayitlar var (needs_recovery: temiz kapatilmamis). Yazilirsa cekirdek baglarken gunlugu yazdiklarimizin uzerine oynatir. Once birimi Linux'ta baglayip duzgun ayirin veya e2fsck ile onarin.`
    - `Bu bir ext gunluk aygiti (journal_dev); dosya sistemi degildir, icine yazilamaz.`
    - `Bu birim su ozellikleri kullaniyor ve bu surumde yazma desteklenmiyor: {}. Yanlis yazip birimi bozmamak icin islem reddedildi.` (was not wrapped in tr() before)
    - `Bu klasor buyuk/kucuk harf duyarsiz (casefold); bu surumde icine ad eklenemez.`
    - `Dizin indeksi bozuk: inode {}`
    - `Klasor degistirilemez (immutable) olarak isaretli.`
    - `Klasorde en fazla {} alt klasor olabilir`
    - `Oge degistirilemez (immutable/append-only) olarak isaretli: {}`
    - `inline_data dizinine yazma desteklenmiyor`
  - extmove.py:
    - `Birimde stable_inodes ozelligi var: inode numaralari degistirilemez. Birimi, silinecek gruplarda dosya kalmayacak boyuta kucultun.`
  
  ### Effect on volumes our own formatter makes
  Nothing breaks. Our ext2/3/4 volumes, including `modern=False`, stay writable and keep the same detected type (checked in r05/r14, and all existing tests pass). Visible differences:
  - Overwriting a file now keeps its mode, uid and gid instead of resetting to 0644 and root.
  - On mke2fs volumes, the fs type shown can change where the old rule was wrong: for example `-O ^extent,^huge_file` with flex_bg is now ext4, not ext3.

GitHub'da iki ayrı test koşusu var; ikisi farklı şeyleri yakalıyor.

**1. Uzun testler (tam profil, şu an sürüyor):** 65 iş başarılı, hata yok; 41 iş sırada ya da koşuyor.
- **Kapsam:** 11 dosya sistemi (FAT12/16/32, exFAT, NTFS, ext2/3/4, HFS+, UDF, XFS), her biri MBR, GPT ve mantıksal bölüm üzerinde.
  - Linux'ta tümü; Windows ve macOS'ta kendi sürücüsünün denetleyebildiği türler.
- **Her senaryo:**
  - Bölüm oluşturulur ve biçimlendirilir.
  - İçine yaklaşık 3.000 küçük dosya, 64–256 MiB'lik orta dosyalar ile 1 GiB ve 5 GiB'lık büyük dosyalar yazılır. FAT32'de tam 4 GiB-1 sınırında bir dosya da var.
  - Ardından sırayla:
    - büyüt, küçült, sağa taşı, sola taşı, geri büyüt;
    - dosya silme/ekleme/ad değiştirme;
    - silinen dosya kurtarma, klonlama;
    - yedek alıp geri yükleme;
    - MBR↔GPT dönüştürme;
    - boş alan silme, kayıp bölüm bulma.
- **Her adımdan sonra üç denetim:**
  - Kendi okuyucumuzla her dosyanın içerik özeti.
  - Harici fsck.
  - İşletim sisteminin kendi sürücüsüyle bağlayıp okuma: Linux'ta `mount`, Windows'ta VHD bağlama + `chkdsk`, macOS'ta `hdiutil` + `fsck`.
- **Ek işler:**
  - Gerçek aygıt yolu: Linux scsi_debug, Windows takılı VHD, macOS hdiutil aygıtı.
  - Gerçek pencere sisteminde arayüz denemesi.
- **Bu turda yeni:** Yedek adımı artık hem tam hem "yalnızca kullanılan alan" yedeğini deniyor ve geri yüklemeyi çöple dolu bir hedefe yapıyor.
- **Sınırı:** Bu testler birimleri hep kendi biçimlendiricimizle üretiyor. picozed hatası da bu yüzden kaçmıştı.

**2. Yabancı girdi matrisi (yeni; ilk tur bitti):**
- **Kapsam:** 68 varyant, her biri 3 farklı tohumla. Birimler gerçek araçlarla (`mkfs.fat`, `mkfs.exfat`, `mkntfs`, `mke2fs`, `mkfs.xfs`, HFS+, UDF, btrfs, F2FS) ve çok çeşitli seçeneklerle üretiliyor, dosyalar Linux çekirdeğiyle yazılıyor.
- **Denenenler:** tür ve etiket tespiti, okuma, iki kipli yedek/geri yükleme, yazma, boyutlandırma. Her biri fsck ve çekirdeğe karşı denetleniyor.
- **İlk turun sonucu:** 8 gruptan 2'si temiz geçti, 6'sında gerçek hatalar çıktı.
  - FAT'te 2048/4096 baytlık sektörde boyutlandırma birimi bozuyor.
  - NTFS'te büyük kümelerde yazma sonrası ntfs-3g birimi bağlamıyor; 4K sektörde dosyalar görünmüyor.
  - ext4 inline_data okumada çöküyor.
  - XFS 1 KiB blokta büyütme birimi bozuyor.
  - HFS+'ta Yunanca ad listede görünmüyor.

**Şimdiki durum:** Bu hatalar ve denetim bulguları için beş düzeltme ajanından dördü bitti (ext, FAT/exFAT, bölüm tabloları, XFS/HFS+); her biri gerçek araçlarla regresyon testi ekledi. NTFS ajanı sürüyor. O bitince hepsini birleştirip yerelde tüm testleri koşturacağım. Sonra matrisi GitHub'da `--tur 10` ile, saatlerce sürecek şekilde yeniden başlatacağım. Yeni regresyon testleri bundan sonra her push'ta CI'da da çalışacak.

{

 "Том не чистый (некорректно отключён, есть запись об ошибке или необработанные осиротевшие inode); его битовым картам нельзя доверять. Сначала проверьте его e2fsck.",
 "该卷不干净（未正常卸载、有错误记录或有未处理的孤立 inode）；其位图不可信。请先用 e2fsck 检查。",
 "ボリュームがクリーンではありません（正しくアンマウントされていない、エラー記録、または未処理の孤立 inode があります）。ビットマップは信頼できません。先に e2fsck で検査してください。",
 "볼륨이 깨끗하지 않습니다(정상적으로 분리되지 않았거나, 오류 기록 또는 처리되지 않은 고아 inode가 있음). 비트맵을 신뢰할 수 없습니다. 먼저 e2fsck로 검사하십시오."],
"Birimde stable_inodes ozelligi var: inode numaralari degistirilemez. Birimi, silinecek gruplarda dosya kalmayacak boyuta kucultun.": [
 "The volume has the stable_inodes feature: inode numbers cannot change. Shrink the volume only to a size where no files remain in the groups to be removed.",
 "Der Datenträger hat die Eigenschaft stable_inodes: Inode-Nummern dürfen sich nicht ändern. Verkleinern Sie ihn nur so weit, dass in den entfernten Gruppen keine Dateien liegen.",
 "Le volume a la fonctionnalité stable_inodes : les numéros d'inode ne peuvent pas changer. Réduisez le volume seulement jusqu'à une taille où aucun fichier ne reste dans les groupes supprimés.",
 "Il volume ha la funzione stable_inodes: i numeri di inode non possono cambiare. Ridurre il volume solo fino a una dimensione in cui nei gruppi rimossi non restino file.",
 "El volumen tiene la característica stable_inodes: los números de inodo no pueden cambiar. Reduzca el volumen solo hasta un tamaño en el que no queden archivos en los grupos eliminados.",
 "У тома есть свойство stable_inodes: номера inode нельзя менять. Уменьшайте том только до размера, при котором в удаляемых группах не остаётся файлов.",
 "该卷启用了 stable_inodes：inode 编号不能改变。只能将卷缩小到要删除的组中没有文件的大小。",
 "このボリュームには stable_inodes 機能があります。inode 番号は変更できません。削除されるグループにファイルが残らないサイズまでのみ縮小してください。",
 "볼륨에 stable_inodes 기능이 있어 inode 번호를 바꿀 수 없습니다. 제거될 그룹에 파일이 남지 않는 크기까지만 축소하십시오."],
"Birimin gunlugunde islenmemis kayitlar var (needs_recovery: temiz kapatilmamis). Yazilirsa cekirdek baglarken gunlugu yazdiklarimizin uzerine oynatir. Once birimi Linux'ta baglayip duzgun ayirin veya e2fsck ile onarin.": [
 "The volume's journal has unprocessed records (needs_recovery: not cleanly unmounted). If written, the kernel would replay the journal over our changes when mounting. First mount the volume in Linux and unmount it properly, or repair it with e2fsck.",
 "Das Journal des Datenträgers enthält unverarbeitete Einträge (needs_recovery: nicht sauber getrennt). Würde geschrieben, spielte der Kernel beim Einhängen das Journal über unsere Änderungen. Hängen Sie den Datenträger zuerst unter Linux ein und sauber aus oder reparieren Sie ihn mit e2fsck.",
 "Le journal du volume contient des enregistrements non traités (needs_recovery : non démonté proprement). En cas d'écriture, le noyau rejouerait le journal par-dessus nos modifications au montage. Montez d'abord le volume sous Linux et démontez-le proprement, ou réparez-le avec e2fsck.",
 "Il journal del volume contiene record non elaborati (needs_recovery: non smontato correttamente). Scrivendo, il kernel al montaggio riapplicherebbe il journal sopra le nostre modifiche. Montare prima il volume in Linux e smontarlo correttamente, oppure ripararlo con e2fsck.",
 "El diario del volumen tiene registros sin procesar (needs_recovery: no se desmontó limpiamente). Si se escribe, el kernel reproduciría el diario sobre nuestros cambios al montarlo. Monte antes el volumen en Linux y desmóntelo correctamente, o repárelo con e2fsck.",
 "В журнале тома есть необработанные записи (needs_recovery: том не был корректно отключён). При записи ядро при монтировании воспроизведёт журнал поверх наших изменений. Сначала смонтируйте том в Linux и корректно отключите его или исправьте e2fsck.",
 "该卷的日志中有未处理的记录（needs_recovery：未正常卸载）。若写入，内核挂载时会在我们的修改之上重放日志。请先在 Linux 中挂载并正常卸载该卷，或用 e2fsck 修复。",
 "ボリュームのジャーナルに未処理のレコードがあります（needs_recovery: 正しくアンマウントされていません）。書き込むと、カーネルはマウント時に変更の上へジャーナルを再生します。先に Linux でマウントして正しくアンマウントするか、e2fsck で修復してください。",
 "볼륨 저널에 처리되지 않은 레코드가 있습니다(needs_recovery: 정상적으로 분리되지 않음). 쓰기를 하면 커널이 마운트할 때 변경 내용 위에 저널을 재생합니다. 먼저 Linux에서 볼륨을 마운트한 뒤 정상적으로 분리하거나 e2fsck로 복구하십시오."],

"Birim coklu baglama korumasi (mmp) kullaniyor; baska bir makinede bagli olabilir. Yazma reddedildi.": [

"Birim temiz degil (temiz kapatilmamis, hata kaydi ya da islenmemis yetim inode var); bitmap'lere guvenilemez. Once e2fsck ile denetleyin.": [
 "The volume is not clean (not cleanly unmounted, has an error record or unprocessed orphan inodes); its bitmaps cannot be trusted. Check it with e2fsck first.",
 "Der Datenträger ist nicht sauber (nicht sauber getrennt, Fehlereintrag oder unverarbeitete verwaiste Inodes); seinen Bitmaps ist nicht zu trauen. Prüfen Sie ihn zuerst mit e2fsck.",
 "Le volume n'est pas propre (non démonté proprement, erreur enregistrée ou inodes orphelins non traités) ; ses bitmaps ne sont pas fiables. Vérifiez-le d'abord avec e2fsck.",
 "Il volume non è pulito (non smontato correttamente, errore registrato o inode orfani non elaborati); le sue bitmap non sono affidabili. Verificarlo prima con e2fsck.",
 "El volumen no está limpio (no se desmontó limpiamente, tiene un error registrado o inodos huérfanos sin procesar); sus mapas de bits no son fiables. Compruébelo antes con e2fsck.",
 "Том не чистый (некорректно отключён, есть запись об ошибке или необработанные осиротевшие inode); его битовым картам нельзя доверять. Сначала проверьте его e2fsck.",
 "该卷不干净（未正常卸载、有错误记录或有未处理的孤立 inode）；其位图不可信。请先用 e2fsck 检查。",
 "ボリュームがクリーンではありません（正しくアンマウントされていない、エラー記録、または未処理の孤立 inode があります）。ビットマップは信頼できません。先に e2fsck で検査してください。",
 "볼륨이 깨끗하지 않습니다(정상적으로 분리되지 않았거나, 오류 기록 또는 처리되지 않은 고아 inode가 있음). 비트맵을 신뢰할 수 없습니다. 먼저 e2fsck로 검사하십시오."],
"Birimde stable_inodes ozelligi var: inode numaralari degistirilemez. Birimi, silinecek gruplarda dosya kalmayacak boyuta kucultun.": [
 "The volume has the stable_inodes feature: inode numbers cannot change. Shrink the volume only to a size where no files remain in the groups to be removed.",
 "Der Datenträger hat die Eigenschaft stable_inodes: Inode-Nummern dürfen sich nicht ändern. Verkleinern Sie ihn nur so weit, dass in den entfernten Gruppen keine Dateien liegen.",
 "Le volume a la fonctionnalité stable_inodes : les numéros d'inode ne peuvent pas changer. Réduisez le volume seulement jusqu'à une taille où aucun fichier ne reste dans les groupes supprimés.",
 "Il volume ha la funzione stable_inodes: i numeri di inode non possono cambiare. Ridurre il volume solo fino a una dimensione in cui nei gruppi rimossi non restino file.",
 "El volumen tiene la característica stable_inodes: los números de inodo no pueden cambiar. Reduzca el volumen solo hasta un tamaño en el que no queden archivos en los grupos eliminados.",
 "У тома есть свойство stable_inodes: номера inode нельзя менять. Уменьшайте том только до размера, при котором в удаляемых группах не остаётся файлов.",
 "该卷启用了 stable_inodes：inode 编号不能改变。只能将卷缩小到要删除的组中没有文件的大小。",
 "このボリュームには stable_inodes 機能があります。inode 番号は変更できません。削除されるグループにファイルが残らないサイズまでのみ縮小してください。",
 "볼륨에 stable_inodes 기능이 있어 inode 번호를 바꿀 수 없습니다. 제거될 그룹에 파일이 남지 않는 크기까지만 축소하십시오."],
"Birimin gunlugunde islenmemis kayitlar var (needs_recovery: temiz kapatilmamis). Yazilirsa cekirdek baglarken gunlugu yazdiklarimizin uzerine oynatir. Once birimi Linux'ta baglayip duzgun ayirin veya e2fsck ile onarin.": [
 "The volume's journal has unprocessed records (needs_recovery: not cleanly unmounted). If written, the kernel would replay the journal over our changes when mounting. First mount the volume in Linux and unmount it properly, or repair it with e2fsck.",
 "Das Journal des Datenträgers enthält unverarbeitete Einträge (needs_recovery: nicht sauber getrennt). Würde geschrieben, spielte der Kernel beim Einhängen das Journal über unsere Änderungen. Hängen Sie den Datenträger zuerst unter Linux ein und sauber aus oder reparieren Sie ihn mit e2fsck.",
 "Le journal du volume contient des enregistrements non traités (needs_recovery : non démonté proprement). En cas d'écriture, le noyau rejouerait le journal par-dessus nos modifications au montage. Montez d'abord le volume sous Linux et démontez-le proprement, ou réparez-le avec e2fsck.",
 "Il journal del volume contiene record non elaborati (needs_recovery: non smontato correttamente). Scrivendo, il kernel al montaggio riapplicherebbe il journal sopra le nostre modifiche. Montare prima il volume in Linux e smontarlo correttamente, oppure ripararlo con e2fsck.",
 "El diario del volumen tiene registros sin procesar (needs_recovery: no se desmontó limpiamente). Si se escribe, el kernel reproduciría el diario sobre nuestros cambios al montarlo. Monte antes el volumen en Linux y desmóntelo correctamente, o repárelo con e2fsck.",
 "В журнале тома есть необработанные записи (needs_recovery: том не был корректно отключён). При записи ядро при монтировании воспроизведёт журнал поверх наших изменений. Сначала смонтируйте том в Linux и корректно отключите его или исправьте e2fsck.",
 "该卷的日志中有未处理的记录（needs_recovery：未正常卸载）。若写入，内核挂载时会在我们的修改之上重放日志。请先在 Linux 中挂载并正常卸载该卷，或用 e2fsck 修复。",
 "ボリュームのジャーナルに未処理のレコードがあります（needs_recovery: 正しくアンマウントされていません）。書き込むと、カーネルはマウント時に変更の上へジャーナルを再生します。先に Linux でマウントして正しくアンマウントするか、e2fsck で修復してください。",
 "볼륨 저널에 처리되지 않은 레코드가 있습니다(needs_recovery: 정상적으로 분리되지 않음). 쓰기를 하면 커널이 마운트할 때 변경 내용 위에 저널을 재생합니다. 먼저 Linux에서 볼륨을 마운트한 뒤 정상적으로 분리하거나 e2fsck로 복구하십시오."],

content.text:
Düzeltmelerin tamamı birleştirildi, yerel testler temiz ve `main`'e push edildi. Yeni commit'in CI'ı ve 10 turluk yabancı girdi matrisi GitHub'da başladı; bu matrisin saatler sürmesini bekliyorum.

Bu turda yapılanlar:
- **Kök neden:** Testler dosya sistemlerini hep kendi biçimlendiricimizle üretiyordu; okuyucu da aynı varsayımla çalıştığı için yanlış varsayım testten geçiyordu. Yazıcılar da yalnızca bilinen sorunları reddediyordu; bilinmeyen durumlarda yazmaya izin veriyorlardı.
- **Bulgular:** Denetim ve yeni matris yaklaşık 45 sorun çıkardı. Hepsi ya düzeltildi ya da güvenli retle kapatıldı: program o birimi bozmak yerine "bu birime yazılamaz" diyor. Kapanan başlıca sorunlar:
  - ext4'te günlüğü işlenmemiş birime yazma ve sabit bağ silerken diğer adı bozma.
  - exFAT'ta Linux/Windows'un oluşturduğu dizinlerde dosyaların kaybolması.
  - NTFS'te Hızlı Başlangıç ile kapatılmış Windows birimine yazma, 4K sektörlü birimlerde yanlış okuma, büyük kümede birimin bağlanamaz hale gelmesi.
  - Bölüm tablosu yazılınca bölüm numaralarının kayması (fstab ve GRUB'u bozar).
  - FAT ve XFS'te boyutlandırmanın birimi bozması.
- **picozed.img:**
  - İçerik referans araçlarla bayt bayt aynı: FAT32'de 4 dosya, ext4'te 4.370 dosya.
  - FAT32 bölümü yapısal olarak bozuk: her iki FAT tablosunun başında eski bir önyükleme sektörünün baytları var. Bu bozulma DiskUltimate'ten gelmiş görünmüyor: dosyalardan önce var ve görüntü projeden eski.
  - Program artık bu bölümü "Yapı tutarsız" olarak gösteriyor, dosyaları okuyor ama yazmayı reddediyor ve yedekte bölümün tamamını alıyor.
- **Testler:** 79 yeni regresyon testi eklendi; hepsi eski kodda başarısız, yeni kodda başarılı ve artık her push'ta CI'da koşuyor. Mevcut paket de temiz: 92/94 (atlanan 2 yalnızca Windows'ta çalışıyor); tanılama, platform, çeviri ve arayüz denetimleri geçiyor.

**Henüz doğrulanmayanlar:** NTFS düzeltmelerinin Windows'un kendi aracı `chkdsk` ile denenmesi (4K sektör, 64 KiB üstü küme, Hızlı Başlangıç kapısı) VirtualBox'taki Windows misafirinde yapılmalı; şu an yalnızca Linux araçlarıyla sınandı. HFS+ yazıcısı adları macOS biçiminde saklıyor; bu yüzden Linux, bizim yazdığımız Yunanca tonoslu adları bulamaz. Bu bilinçli bir tercih.

Eski koddaki uzun test koşusu bitince (şu an 83 başarılı, hata yok) uzun testleri yeni kodla yeniden başlatacağım. Sonuçları gelince bildireceğim.

    from diskultimate.core.xfs import XfsFS
    from diskultimate.core.xfsgrow import xfs_grow
    mkfs, repair = _tool("mkfs.xfs"), _tool("xfs_repair")
    root = _work(f"xfs_{tag}_kaynak")
    shutil.rmtree(root, ignore_errors=True)
    expected = _xfs_tree(root)
    img = _work(f"xfs_{tag}.img")
    if os.path.exists(img):
        os.unlink(img)
    with open(img, "wb") as fh:
        fh.truncate(320 * MIB)
    # agsize=100m: 3 tam + 20 MiB'lik kisa son AG -> hem uzatma hem yeni AG
    r = subprocess.run([mkfs, "-q", "-f", *opts, "-d", "agsize=100m", "-p", root, img],

    with open(img, "r+b") as fh:
        fh.truncate(900 * MIB)
    d = DiskImage(img)
    try:
        plan = xfs_grow(d, 900 * MIB)
    finally:
        d.close()
    assert plan["new_agcount"] > plan["old_agcount"], plan
    r = subprocess.run([repair, "-n", "-f", img], capture_output=True, text=True)

    d = DiskImage(img, readonly=True)
    try:

        for path, data in expected.items():
            assert fs.read_file(path) == data, (tag, path)
    finally:
        d.close()
    os.unlink(img)
    shutil.rmtree(root, ignore_errors=True)

def _encode_runs(runs: List[Tuple[int, int]]) -> bytes:
    """(lcn, kume) listesini NTFS veri kosullarina cevirir."""
    out = bytearray()
    prev = 0
    for lcn, count in runs:
        delta = lcn - prev
        prev = lcn

input.summary: New NTFS bug: kernel can't list our new dir (64K+)
input.message: New finding from the GitHub foreign-input matrix (10 rounds, latest code incl. your fixes + my same-dir hard-link fix in ntfswrite._names_of): on ntfs-c64k (mkntfs -c 65536) and ntfs-c2m (-c 2097152) — every round — after our write step the Linux kernel ntfs3 driver (mount -t ntfs3 ro) does NOT list the files inside the directory WE created: `access.mkdir("/yeni_dizin")` then write_stream of 6 files `/yeni_dizin/yeni_0.bin` … `yeni_4.bin` (sizes 0, 1, 4096, 300000, 3 MiB+17) and `/yeni_dizin/sonradan.dat`. Kernel check message: "surucu dosyayi listede de gostermiyor" for all 6 (the directory itself exists). Our reader lists and reads them correctly and `ntfsfix -n` passes. Files written into pre-existing (kernel-created) directories and the root ARE visible to the kernel. Variants ntfs-varsayilan (4K), ntfs-c512 and ntfs-s4096 pass all 10 rounds. So the bug is specific to directories created by our mkdir when cluster size > index block size (4096). Strong suspects: the $INDEX_ROOT header field "clusters per index block" (when index_block_size < cluster_size it must be index_block_size/512, with VCNs in 512-byte units — compare with the $INDEX_ROOT of the root directory mkntfs created on a -c 65536 volume, which ntfs3 reads fine), the index block size field, and/or $INDEX_ALLOCATION/$BITMAP sizing/VCN units once the dir overflows into an index block. Please fix in ntfswrite/ntfsindex (and the formatter if it shares the code), add a regression test that compares every $INDEX_ROOT/$INDEX_ALLOCATION header field of a directory created by our mkdir against mkntfs's root dir on -c 512/4096/65536/2097152 volumes (and, if possible, populate with ntfscp into our new dir and check `ntfsls -p /yeni_dizin` lists everything — ntfsls uses libntfs which may be laxer than ntfs3, so the field comparison matters most). Run regress_ntfs + run_all NTFS tests individually + platform_check. Don't commit. Report the root cause and the fix briefly.

ntfs3 hidden-directory bug (-c 65536 / -c 2097152) is fixed; nothing is committed. I can't mount here, so please re-run the GitHub matrix with ntfs3 to confirm the kernel lists the directory.

ROOT CAUSE: byte 0x0C of $INDEX_ROOT ("clusters per index block").
- When the cluster is larger than the 4 KiB index block, NTFS counts this field in 512-byte units, so it must be 8 (mkntfs and Windows write 8).
- We wrote max(1, index_size // cluster_size) = 1.
- ntfs3's indx_init rejects the index when index_block_size != index_block_clst*512, so it treats the directory as empty.
- ntfs-3g and our own reader ignore this field, so `ntfsfix -n` passed.
- On 512 B and 4 KiB clusters the value was already right, which is why only the large-cluster variants failed.

The same bug was in our own formatter: root dir, $Secure $SII/$SDH, $Extend and the $ObjId/$Quota/$Reparse roots. So our own 64K-cluster volumes were affected too.

A second difference: $INDEX_ALLOCATION data_size was the whole cluster (64 KiB or 2 MiB, with a 64-byte $BITMAP). mkntfs uses blocks×4096; the allocated size stays a multiple of the cluster.

FIX:
- ntfs.py: new index_block_clusters(index_size, cluster_size), returning index//cluster when the block is at least a cluster, else index//512. All formatter index roots use it, and the formatter root's $INDEX_ALLOCATION data_size is now one block.
- ntfswrite._rebuild_index_root (used by mkdir) uses the same helper.
- ntfsindex._install_allocation: data_size is one block.
- ntfsindex._grow_allocation: data_size grows block by block and uses the spare space in the last cluster before taking new clusters. Directories written by older versions (data_size = cluster) still work.

Every header field of a directory made by our mkdir now matches mkntfs's root on -c 512/4096/65536/2097152.

TESTS (in tests/regress_ntfs.py):
- t20_kendi_dizinimiz_indeks_alanlari_mkntfs_ile_ayni: on those four cluster sizes, compares $INDEX_ROOT and $INDEX_ALLOCATION/$BITMAP fields of our directory (60 files, so it spills into INDX blocks) and of an empty directory against the mkntfs root. It then adds 40 more files with ntfscp into /yeni_dizin, runs ntfsfix -n, and checks that ntfsls and our reader both list all 100.
- t21_bicimlendirici_buyuk_kume_indeks_alanlari: our formatter at 64K; root/$SII/$SDH/$Extend fields must be 8, then mkdir + 60 files must pass ntfsfix and ntfsls.
- Both fail on HEAD with "blok_kume: mkntfs 8, bizim 1".
- I renamed mine to t20/t21 because your t19 hard-link test sits in the same file.

RESULTS:
- regress_ntfs: 21/21 pass, including your t19.
- run_all NTFS tests run individually (t17, t23, t35, t36, t42, t56, t57, t75, t77, t84, t85): all pass.
- platform_check: 0 findings.
- No new tr() strings.

Files changed this round: src/diskultimate/core/ntfs.py, ntfswrite.py, ntfsindex.py, tests/regress_ntfs.py.

Still needs a Windows chkdsk on a 64K-cluster volume from our formatter and on directories we create there.
</agent-message>
